source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives sharp two-arm variance bounds under fixed marginals and identifies the upper covariance endpoint through the comonotone coupling.
The article is the cited 2023 JRSSB multi-arm design-based framework and uses general treatment contrasts in its finite-population analysis.
Tchen establishes the fixed-marginal concordance/supermodular ordering used as the rearrangement ingredient.
The paper proposes integer programming to compute a worst-case potential-outcome copula for broad randomization designs and linear- or quadratic-in-treatment estimators.
The paper casts causal partial identification with K potential-outcome margins as MOT, obtains exact identified sets, and extends its convergence result to general quadratic objectives.
The paper gives a polynomial QAP case in which the identity is optimal for a Robinson similarity/dissimilarity pair when one matrix is Toeplitz.
The paper develops causal-bootstrap inference for the ATE under completely randomized and related designs, using a two-arm least-favourable completion construction.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a short standalone derivation showing precisely how the Zhao-Ding covariance identity turns the loss into a pairwise supermodular quadratic objective, separating the inherited Tchen step from the new cone and Loewner classifications.

For the kernel question, first establish either a polynomial recognition subcone or a complexity barrier for the unrestricted orbit problem; then state the algorithmic target on the strongest tractable realizable subclass.
Add a finite-sample implementation corollary specifying how empirical arm marginals, ties, and a user-supplied PSD loss W yield the O(K²) certificate used by causal-bootstrap software.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0: prove the complete-randomization cone and Loewner theorems, while retaining the realizable-kernel recognition problem as the substantive open extension.
